results.operating_point: builtin-heuristic native verdict (analyze_text); no score threshold
results.method: Deterministic builtin-heuristic detector at its native operating point over (a) 66 original human-authored out-of-domain texts in 11 slices, (b) 30 seeded synthetic formulaic-template texts (stress probe only, not LLM output, no TPR claim), (c) cached rows of the six document caches truncated to 5/10/20/40/60/80/120/200 words plus full length (deterministic source_id-sorted sample, max 200 per class per slice), and (d) a refusal matrix across engine/detector/execute_detector/config/API/CLI/bundle layers. Rates are Wilson 95% CIs (z=1.96). AUROC is Mann-Whitney U with 0.5 for ties; AUPRC is step average precision. Both are computed from scratch in this script (no sklearn) and self-tested on known cases.

evidence.explanation: Very uniform sentence lengths can be a weak machine-like signal.
Uniform paragraph sizes can indicate templated prose.
Repeated sentence openings can indicate formulaic structure.
Dense explicit transitions can make prose read formulaically.
Common AI-associated stock phrases are present.
Repeated three-word sequences can indicate templated phrasing.
Lower lexical variety can be a weak signal, but depends strongly on genre.
A low share of one-off words can indicate repetitive vocabulary.
Low punctuation variety can accompany syntactically uniform prose.

notes: W8 worker E qualification probe. Out-of-domain and short-text results are measurements, not claims: per-slice n is small (n=6 per OOD slice), so Wilson uppers are wide and the pooled OOD number must not be read as a supported FPR claim. The lyrics slice is near-domain (RAID covers poetry) and is flagged as such. Japanese texts have no whitespace, so the detector's word counter sees 16-20 words per text (runs split by punctuation) instead of the ~140 whitespace words; the 6/6 abstention on that slice is a length-gate effect on a spaceless script, not a language judgement. The same whitespace-word artefact affects the short-text truncation: 49 of the 400 sampled DetectRL-X rows are Chinese with fewer than 20 whitespace words at full length, so truncating them to a 5/10/20-word budget keeps the full (long) text and they receive normal verdicts — that is why DetectRL-X abstention is 0.963/0.948/0.905 at the 5/10/20-word budgets instead of 1.000. A whitespace-word budget is not a length control for spaceless scripts; the DetectRL-X small-budget numbers must be read with that caveat. No threshold was tuned; no failing case was dropped.
